newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says won't touch pensions till '98.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says won't touch pensions till '98.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday he would not touch pensions until 1998 in accordance with a pension reform deal reached last year.

"I have taken the decision not to touch pensions until 1998 and to start straight away in 1997 with a big discussion between employers and unions on pensions and the whole welfare state," Prodi told a news conference.
"The accords will be respected," he said.
Prodi last week asked a special body monitoring pension spending to carry out a study of the impact of potential changes to current regulations.

Trade union leaders, backed by the hard left Communist Refoundation party that ensures the government's majority in parliament, have fiercely rejected suggestions that changes to the system be brought forward and have threatened mass protests.
Economic analysts have criticised the 1995 pension reform, enacted by then prime minister Lamberto Dini, for being too slow in moving to eradicate generous early retirement packages.

Commentators have said Italy needs to restructure pensions spending to balance its books and get the ratio between the state deficit and gross domestic product below the three percent level needed to join Europe's planned single currency.
